issue: The figure visually encodes a strict one-to-one mapping (one dashed arrow from each workload dimension to exactly one architectural decision), while the caption explicitly says the arrows are non-exclusive and gives an example of a cross-influence (Latency SLO shaping both model choice and serving configuration) that the figure does not draw.

The arrows are non-exclusive: in practice a dimension often influences several decisions at once (e.g. latency SLO shapes both model choice and serving configuration)'. Figure: exactly six left boxes, six right boxes, and six single dashed arrows; 'Latency SLO' points only to 'TTFT/TPOT & batch window', not to 'model size / type'.
acceptance_test: Either add at least one cross-arrow (e.g. Latency SLO → model size / type) or add an in-figure note such as 'primary mapping shown; cross-influences omitted' so the drawn encoding no longer contradicts the caption's non-exclusive claim.

issue: The figure title says 'canonical 70B FP16', but the QLoRA bar is explicitly 4-bit NF4, not FP16. The title therefore mislabels the precision of one of the three scenarios.
evidence: Title: 'Memory floor: inference vs fine-tuning (canonical 70B FP16)'. Figure note: 'QLoRA: 4-bit (NF4) base + LoRA adapters + a small optimizer.' Caption: 'QLoRA fits ~50–70 GB on a single GPU.'
acceptance_test: Retitle to 'canonical 70B model (FP16 unless noted)' or '70B memory floor across precision/state scenarios'; verify the title no longer implies all three bars are FP16.

issue: The figure and caption label the 989 TFLOPS plateau as 'dense (no sparsity) FP16', but 989 TFLOPS is the sparse FP16 datasheet peak; dense FP16 is ~494.5 TFLOPS. The ridge points (295 and 206) are therefore computed from a sparse peak while claiming dense.
evidence: Caption: 'dense (no sparsity) FP16; the ceilings are peak/theoretical datasheet values'. Chart: 'compute plateau = 989 TFLOPS', 'ridge ≈ 295', 'ridge ≈ 206'. NVIDIA H100 datasheet: 989 TFLOPS FP16 with sparsity, 494.5 TFLOPS dense.
acceptance_test: Either relabel as sparse FP16 and remove 'dense (no sparsity)' from the caption, or replot with 494.5 TFLOPS dense: H100 ridge ≈ 148 FLOP/byte, H200 ridge ≈ 103 FLOP/byte; update all dependent text and the prefill/decode classification if needed.

issue: The formula annotation says 'O = 300 output per turn', but the plotted 34.0 GB bar and the caption use a single final 300-token output. If 300 output tokens were added per turn, the total would be 13,860 tokens and ~36.3 GB, not 34.0 GB.
evidence: Figure 19.3 formula line: 'append-only total = I0 + T·δ + T·γ + O_final @ 2.62 MB/token (I0 = 9.2K input, δ = 800 retrieved, γ = 65 generated, O = 300 output per turn)'. The bar is labeled 34.0 GB. Recompute with O per turn: 9,200 + 4×800 + 4×65 + 4×300 = 13,860 tokens; 13,860 × 2.62 MB ≈ 36.3 GB. Recompute with one final output: 9,200 + 4×800 + 4×65 + 300 = 12,960 tokens; 12,960 × 2.62 MB ≈ 34.0 GB. The caption also says 'one final 300-token answer'.
acceptance_test: Change the annotation to 'O_final = 300 output once (final answer)' or equivalent, and verify the displayed 34.0 GB equals (9,200 + 4×800 + 4×65 + 300) × 2.62 MB.

issue: The figure note claims 'processed tokens grow ~2.5x under no prefix reuse', but the figure's own per-turn retained-context arithmetic implies a much larger summed per-call processed-token growth.
evidence: Figure 19.2 note: 'Bars are RETAINED context/KV, not summed per-call processed or billed tokens; processed tokens grow ~2.5x under no prefix reuse'. Using the figure's own values, summed per-call processed tokens for turns 0–4 are 9,500 + 10,365 + 11,230 + 12,095 + 12,960 = 56,150; versus 9,500 single-shot, that is ~5.9x, not ~2.5x. Excluding output tokens gives 54,650 / 9,200 ≈ 5.9x. The ~2.5x figure is not reproducible from the displayed model.
acceptance_test: Recompute the summed per-call processed-token ratio from the figure's own turn-by-turn values and either correct '~2.5x' to the derived value (~5.9x) or explicitly state the different denominator/scope that yields ~2.5x.

issue: The explanatory note and legend under the two panels are set in very small type and are dense; at print size the note is difficult to read and easy to skip, even though it carries essential scope caveats (retained context vs processed/billed tokens).
evidence: Rendered page 327 shows the note 'counterfactual: each column = a separate completion after T turns...' and the legend labels at a much smaller size than the caption and body text. The note spans the figure width and contains critical semantic qualifications.
acceptance_test: Increase the figure note and legend type to at least 8 pt at final print size, or move the scope caveat into the caption/body text, then re-render and confirm legibility at 100% print scale.

figure: Figure 19.2 — Agent turns: token and KV growth (printed p. 307)
issue: In-figure note makes a quantitative claim ('processed tokens grow ~2.5x under no prefix reuse') that cannot be rederived from the figure's own stated inputs; every reconstruction from the figure's arithmetic gives a different factor.
evidence: Figure inputs (legend + caption + p.305 formula): I0=9,200; delta=800/turn; gamma=65/turn; O=300 final. Per-turn processed under no prefix reuse: turn 0 = 9,500; turn 4 = 9,200+4*800+4*65+300 = 12,960 -> ratio 12,960/9,500 = 1.36x (also = KV ratio 34.0/24.9 = 1.37x). Cumulative processed turns 0..4 = 56,150 -> 5.9x. Turns 1..4 = 46,650 -> 4.9x. None equals ~2.5x. Table 19-1 / A-04 not on this page: NOT VERIFIED as source.

Re-render and confirm the note's number matches an independent recomputation from I0/delta/gamma/O.

figure: Figure 19.3 — State-management policy at four agent turns (printed p. 308)
issue: Internal semantic contradiction inside the figure: the formula counts the 300-token output once (O_final), but the same figure's parameter glossary labels it 'per turn', which would change the derived 34.0 GB result.
evidence: Figure formula line: 'append-only total = I0 + T*delta + T*gamma + O_final @ 2.62 MB/token'. Parameter glossary on the same figure: '(I0 = 9.2K input, delta = 800 retrieved, gamma = 65 generated, O = 300 output per turn)'. If O were truly per turn at T=4: 9,200+3,200+260+1,200 = 13,860 tokens x 2.62 MB = 36.3 GB, contradicting the printed 34.0 GB bar, the caption ('9,200 input + 300 output + 800 + 65 per turn'), and p.305 ('I0 + T*delta + T*gamma + O_final = 9,200 + 800T + 65T + 300'). Correct reading: O_final = 300 once, total 12,960 x 2.62 MB = 33.96 GB ~= 34.0 GB.
acceptance_test: Change the glossary to 'O_final = 300 final output (once)' (or move 'per turn' to cover only delta and gamma), rebuild the PDF, and confirm the formula, glossary, caption, bar value 34.0 GB, and p.305 arithmetic all yield 12,960 tokens / 34.0 GB from one shared parameter set.

issue: The 'generated (gamma=65)' stack segment is ~0.5% of bar height and is effectively invisible at print size, so a legend entry exists for a component the reader cannot see or distinguish.

issue: Figure 7.6 caption fixes the 70B inference floor at '~165 GB (weights + KV, max 9.5K)', while Chapter 8 fixes the SAME 70B model's context at 'canonical 9.2K'. The identical model's context length is stated as two different rounded values across chapters.
evidence: Printed Fig 7.6 caption (p.122): 'weights + KV, max 9.5K'. Printed prose: p.137 Fig 8.2 caption 'the plotted prefill (9.2K input)'; p.138 'the canonical 9.2K context, FP16 full-MHA'; p.145 'at the canonical 9.2K context' / 'at the canonical 9.2K point'. figure: Fig 19.3 — State-management policy at turn 4 (printed p.308 / batch 328)
issue: Internal inconsistency in the in-figure formula gloss. The equation line reads 'append-only total = I0 + T*delta + T*gamma + O_final' (one-time final output), but the parenthetical gloss immediately below reads 'O = 300 output per turn'. Taken literally ('per turn') the term becomes T*O, contradicting both the equation's own O_final term and the plotted Append-only bar value (34.0 GB).
evidence: One-time O_final at T=4: 9,200 + 4*800 + 4*65 + 300 = 12,960 tokens * 2.62 MB = 33.96 GB ~= 34.0 GB (matches the Append-only bar, Fig 19.2 turn-4, prose p.305, and Fig 19.3 caption '9,200 input + 300 output + 800 + 65 per turn'). Literal per-turn O: 9,200 + 3,200 + 260 + 4*300 = 13,860 tokens * 2.62 = 36.3 GB != 34.0 GB. The 'per turn' qualifier on O is the sole inconsistent element; equation, bar, and caption all treat 300 as one-time.
acceptance_test: Recompute append-only total at T=4 with a single final 300-token answer (=12,960 tokens = 34.0 GB), edit the gloss to 'O_final = 300 (one final answer)' removing 'per turn', and confirm the 34.0 GB bar is unchanged.

figure: Fig 19.2 — Token growth vs KV growth, panel (a) (printed p.307 / batch 327)
issue: Grayscale distinguishability: two stacked-bar series use a plain solid fill with no hatch/marker — 'generated (gamma=65)' (tan) and 'output (O=300)' (green). On a grayscale print these two light fills of similar lightness may be near-indistinguishable; only hue and legend order separate them.
evidence: Legend swatches: initial context = blue diagonal-hatch, retrieved = teal dot-pattern, generated = solid tan, output = solid green. The two dominant series (initial, retrieved) carry distinct textures; the two thin top series (generated, output) are both solid. Grayscale collapse of similar-lightness hues is the risk. Mitigation present: explicit legend labels plus stack position (output is topmost).
acceptance_test: Render panel (a) in pure grayscale at print size; if 'generated' and 'output' segments remain separable (via position/legend) accept, otherwise add a distinct hatch/marker to one segment and close.

acceptance_test: Render the page in pure grayscale; the 'append K/V' box and the 'read for attention' box must be distinguishable by fill luminance or border style without relying on color, or the caption must state they share a color class.

issue: Grayscale distinguishability: the Inference bar (blue) and the QLoRA bar (green) fall in similar mid-gray luminance ranges; color is the primary visual differentiator between them. The orange band is at the threshold of visibility and is not reliably distinguishable from the adjacent 'retrieved (δ=800)' dotted-green and 'output (O=300)' solid-green segments, so the four-component decomposition the legend promises is not actually readable in the rendered bars.
